text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000523 bills 99215 at roughly ten times the expected rate, mostly on patients with few or no chronic conditions; the small set of returned charts supports the billed level but is too thin to clear the pattern.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share holds across every complexity stratum, including visits with zero chronic conditions. Sampled 99215 claims there carry simple diagnoses such as abdominal pain (C0277180, C0277333), upper respiratory infection (C0277233, C0277420), UTI (C0277232) and follow-up codes (C0277258), which is the concern rather than a sicker panel. The returned charts point the other way, since all 8 documented 99215 claims were supported. But records came back for under 5% of claims, which is too thin to offset the claim-level pattern. Some notes may also be inflated: C0277491, a single-condition hypertension and follow-up visit, is documented as high MDM at 50 minutes. A third of the notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review have no lab or test line on the claim, which is weak evidence that notes may be templated rather than reflecting what happened. A reviewer should first request a larger chart sample focused on 0–1 condition 99215 visits. Those notes should be checked for cloned or templated language, and the documented data review and time compared against orders, results and scheduling records."}
